title: Specialization, Diversity, and Scaling in Child-Scale Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.36679v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern language models are trained on far more language than children experience, but we know much less about learning from small, naturalistic datasets. We train small GPT-2 models on transcripts of speech with children from dense home recordings (BabyView) and on synthetic child-directed dialogue (TinyDialogues), varying the amount, source, and diversity of training data. Models trained on one child's language environment predict that environment substantially better than other children's environments. Much of this specialization is lexical and distributional: a simple 5-gram model reproduces the cross-child pattern (r=.91). Training on data from multiple children clearly improves prediction of pooled held-out language relative to training on a single child's input without a similarly clear improvement on grammatical benchmarks. Across data sizes, naturalistic and synthetic training inputs also produce different grammatical and lexic

translated_title: 儿童尺度语言模型中的专业化、多样性与规模化
translated_abstract: 现代语言模型训练所用的语言数据远超儿童实际接触的语言量，但我们对从小型自然语言数据集中学习的过程知之甚少。我们在来自密集家庭录音的儿童语音转录文本和合成的儿童导向对话数据上训练小型GPT-2模型，并改变训练数据的数量、来源和多样性。在单个儿童语言环境数据上训练的模型，对该环境的预测效果显著优于对其他儿童环境的预测。这种专业化很大程度上体现在词汇和分布层面：一个简单的5-gram模型就能重现这种跨儿童的模式（r=.91）。与仅在单个儿童输入上训练相比，在多个儿童的数据上训练能明显提升对汇总保留语言的预测，但在语法基准测试上却没有出现类似的明显提升。在不同的数据规模下，自然数据和合成训练数据也会产生不同的语法和词汇表现。
tldr: 在儿童尺度数据上训练的小型语言模型会对单个儿童的语言环境产生词汇和分布层面的专业化，多儿童数据训练虽能提升对汇总语言的预测，但对语法能力的提升并不明显。
en_tdlr: Small language models trained on child-scale data specialize lexically and distributionally to individual children's language environments, and while multi-child training data improves prediction of pooled language, it shows no clear gains on grammatical benchmarks.
